newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 2.

text.p: - This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- GENCOR MAY SPLIT AND FLOAT METALS ARM IN LONDON

South African mining group Gencor is reported to be considering a split into two divisions and the floatation of its base metals operations on the London stock exchange. Gencor is South Africa's second biggest mining group, and is valued on the Johannesburg stock exchange at 4.6 billion stg. The company has said only that it is considering schemes to give it access to international capital markets so that it can fund growth plans.
-- COMPANY DOCTORS CALLED TO HEAL 2,000 BUSINESSES A YEAR

A survey carried out on behalf of the Society of Practitioners in Insolvency has found that over 2,000 British companies turn to company doctors every year for help in cutting costs, restructuring debt and improving management controls. The survey, the first to conducted of the secretive world of corporate 'intensive care', found that among those seeking help were 130 listed companies.
-- ANDERSEN CANDIDATE REJECTED

Andersen Worldwide, the world's largest professional services organisation, is facing boardroom turmoil after the company's partners rejected the board's recommended candidate to succeed the current chief executive. The board is expected Monday to put forward George Shaheen, managing partner of Andersen's global consultancy business, as its preferred candidate after their first choice, Jim Wadia, failed to secure the two-thirds majority of the votes needed.
-- GOVERNMENT TO DETAIL NEW INITIATIVES

The new Labour government is expected this week to unveil details of initiatives aimed at improving the performance of British industry and tackling unemployment. Prime minister Tony Blair is to outline plans for tackling the problems of 'the workless class', while trade secretary Margaret Beckett will announce proposals to consult business leaders on ways to improve Britain's competitiveness.
-- TRANSMITTER SALE HELPS BBC AMASS 500 MILLION STG

The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) is expected to reveal a strong balance sheet when it publishes its annual report next month. The BBC has amassed cash reserves of some 500 million stg, boosted by the 244 million stg sale of its transmitter systems and savings of more than 100 million stg. Most of the money has been earmarked for the development of digital television services.
-- BT CHIEF AND EXECUTIVES SUED FOR 5 MILLION STG

Sir Ian Vallance, chairman of British Telecom, is being sued along with eight BT executives for more than 5 million stg. The High Court case is being brought by Derek Taylor, a small businessman, who alleges that executives working for BT's telephone directory business Yellow Pages conspired with Vallance to operate a policy designed to prevent direct competition with BT.
-- WARNER SEEKS NEW LONDON SITE

Warner Bros, the US film studio, has announced that it has abandoned the planned site in Uxbridge, west London, on which it was to develop a 225 million stg film studio and movie theme park. The company and its UK partner, United News and Media, are now considering about 40 sites around London for the project after dropping the Uxbridge site because of planning difficulties.
-- BT SERVICE FOR HONG KONG

British Telecom has pledged to launch a virtual private network (VPN) service in Hong Kong by the end of next month. The move, which will make BT one of the first foreign operators to launch such a service, follows the issuing of 14 licences by Hong Kong last week. Hong Kong agreed to deregulate VPN's as part of its move towards liberalisation agreed during the World Trade Organisation accord on telecoms.
-- SINGTEL EARNINGS AHEAD BY 11.6 PER CENT

Singapore Telecommunications has announced an 11.6 per cent increase in annual net profit, from S$1.49 billion to S$1.66 billion (US$1.16 billion). The results, which were broadly in line with expectations, came despite SingTel losing the first part of its monopoly during the year. SingTel saw international direct dial traffic increase by 12.5 per cent, helping to offset narrowed profit margins due to tariff cuts.
-- ENERGIS'S FUTURE STILL IN DOUBT

The future for Energis, the telecommunications business owned by UK electricity distribution company National Grid, is still unclear after National Grid said it would not be giving details of its plans for Energis when it announces its results on Tuesday. National Grid said it was still considering 'a number of options', including floatation, for Energis, which is not expected to be profitable before 1999.
